title: Proof Architecture in the OpenAI Lean Library: Representation, Locality, and Semantic Transport
review_process: Three parallel internal critical reviews, root synthesis and edits, followed by mathematical, editorial and rendered-PDF rechecks. Review agents previously contributed to the manuscript; this is not blind or external peer review.
verdict: Ready for submission as a specialist expository/comparative formalization review.
rating_interpretation: Qualitative editorial judgments for this manuscript type, not an acceptance probability or a weighted statistical score. Before scores are included only where a reviewer recorded a comparable baseline.

ratings.reason: The omitted draw-width premise, squared-norm wording and graph inner-product convention are corrected. Source bodies and hypotheses were rechecked; the rating is for the exposition, not a full upstream proof build.
The actual Mahler forms, Crouzeix zero-mode normalization, Fourier identity and positive-block calculation are now explicit.

ratings.category: Novelty of the review and synthesis
ratings.reason: A useful cross-case synthesis and original exposition, including a composed success-budget example. It does not establish a new theorem or a historically new verification method.
Direct comparison with Anatomy of a Formal Proof and specification-driven development; explicit attribution of the classical trace-cone mathematics.
The unit of comparison, exploratory selection trail, actual omitted candidates and difference between inventory and deep reading are specified.

ratings.category: Clarity, natural prose and reader value
ratings.reason: The all-seams construction has a plain-language roadmap, routine compiler description is tighter, and the new budget example connects abstract interfaces to a finite calculation.

168 retained upstream files have pinned byte identities; five original Lean lemmas compile, and exact Python checks reproduce the illustrative results. The proof of the composed budget remains prose rather than a full Lean formalization.

All 38 entries are cited and have retained primary identity evidence; 24 published scholarly DOI records, one preprint, one technical report and 12 source/software records. Two genuine preprints were updated to their published versions.
The 23-page PDF builds without recorded LaTeX problems; overview rows, equations, footnotes and references passed rendered inspection.

resolved_findings.fix: Added Fits depth and bit-width hypotheses to the bounded sampling-loss estimate.
Corrected the projection-budget prose to sums of squared norms.
Distinguished the global counting inner product from normalized conditional fiber averages.
Separated raw counts from normalized laws on different-sized spaces; added a cross-multiplied-count Lean lemma.
Added the composed success-budget proposition, explicit failure semantics, trial budget and tight 640/1024 tape fixture.
Updated documentation to match five compiled lemmas.
Made b_0=1, Hermitian zero coefficients and the exact Fourier-energy normalization explicit.
Defined the actual Mahler forms and d^c convention, and explained horizontal cancellation.
Used a boundary one-form counterexample and distinguished ambient derivatives from intrinsic pullbacks.
Added the short positive-block trace calculation.
Removed an unsupported comparative adjective about corpus breadth.
Compared the review directly with the closest proof-anatomy and specification-driven-development literature.
Explained the actual exploratory selection trail and named omitted endpoints; used the precise pi irrationality-exponent label.
Attributed the ideal weights, cut topology and scalar limits to Elliott-Robert-Santiago Sections 3.1-3.2.
Added the marked-surface construction roadmap, including a genus-zero disk for each fresh strip.
Turned the comparative conclusions into an operational sequence for reading preservation interfaces.
Compressed routine compiler exposition while retaining the probability, representation and cost distinctions.
Updated Anatomy of a Formal Proof and LeanArchitect to verified published metadata, including the latter author order.

strengths: Six detailed preservation chains rather than a catalogue of endpoint theorem names
Concrete counterexamples explain why weaker interfaces fail
A reusable composed accuracy/uniformity/execution argument with a tight exact fixture
Primary-source anchors and portable original examples
remaining_limits: Case selection is purposive and exploratory, not an exhaustive or representative corpus survey.
The review contributes comparative synthesis and explanatory mathematics; historical rarity and a new verification method are not established.
Complete upstream headline theorems and their Comparator configurations have not been independently built by this review.
The composed success-budget proposition is proved in prose; the executable Lean results cover the five named supporting lemmas.
The article remains technically dense and is aimed at mathematicians and formalization researchers.
optional_future_research: Formalize the complete composed success-budget theorem, including finite probability and tape fibers.
Evaluate the preservation framework prospectively on independently selected formalizations.
Add full upstream build evidence where the source toolchains and resources permit it.

exact_example_checks: all 1024 physical tapes and all four event indicators in the tight success-budget fixture
validation.citation_audit_scope: Retained primary identities, DOI/title matches, source artifact identity and source-level claim-support reviews. Metadata identity is distinct from validation of every argument in a cited work.
